newsitem.title: CANADA: Placer says gold reserves, output rising.
newsitem.headline: Placer says gold reserves, output rising.

text.p: Canadian mining company Placer Dome Inc said on Wednesday that its gold reserves rose sharply in 1996 and it forecast a jump in gold production for 1997.
Placer said its estimate of gold ore reserves rose to 26.5 million ounces at the end of 1996, up from 21 million a year earlier.
The company expected to produce 2.3 million ounces of gold in 1997 at an average cost of US$240 an ounce, up from 1.9 million ounces at a cost of US$235 an ounce in 1996.
Capital expenditures were forecast to rise to US$550 million in 1997 from US$416 million in 1996.

The company this month signed an accord to develop the US$576 million Las Cristinas mine in Venezuela. The start of construction depends on granting of environmental permits, tax relief on project materials and finalisation of financing.

Placer said these were "all expected in a matter of months." Construction was due to begin late last year but was delayed until a Venezuelan state-owned mining concern, Placer's partner in the project, signed the project agreement.
Placer projected 1997 exploration spending at US$120 million, up from US$117 million in 1996.
Placer said two new mines, Pipeline in the United States and Musselwhite in Canada, were under budget and ahead of schedule. Commercial production on both mines would begin in April.
Production costs would fall after 1997, "reflecting lower average costs at new mines," Placer said.

Placer said the most significant factors behind its higher gold reserves were the inclusion of Las Cristinas after a positive feasbility study, a reserve increase at the Porgera mine in Papua New Guinea and Placer's higher stake in Porgera.
